fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase HEA is inconsistent with the target as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy containing FCC and B2 phases.
The intervention is Ta addition plus multistage processing rather than intermediate-temperature aging near 600-750°C.
The hypothesis omits the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition and instead predicts only generic toughness improvement.
No quantitative exposure window, aging duration, loading mode, or toughness metric is defined.
The proposed coherent-precipitation mechanism does not address L12 ordering, antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged FCC/B2 boundaries, or ductile transition zones.
The cited evidence concerns compositionally distinct refractory alloys and does not demonstrate preservation of post-aging toughness in the proposed material.
The experiment combines alloying and thermomechanical processing, so it cannot identify which intervention causes any observed difference.
explanation: The response addresses the broad theme of improving HEA mechanical performance after heating, but it reconstructs neither the material system nor the aging-induced mechanism. E1 provides limited precedent for Ta-enabled coherent precipitation and elevated-temperature strength in a tungsten-based alloy, not evidence for post-exposure toughness or the claimed mechanism in the stated HEA; E2 is largely irrelevant. The comparison could test an overall processing package, but its unspecified thermal/loading conditions, absence of mechanism-specific measurements, and confounding of Ta addition with multistage processing make it weakly discriminating. A target-aligned falsification test would compare aging temperatures across roughly 550-750°C and determine whether minimum ductility near 600°C coincides with enhanced L12 ordering, planar-slip pile-ups, and crack initiation at jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips, followed by recovery near 750°C.
